reasoning: The extract has four lines, none carrying a citation (references and links blocks are empty). It describes monitoring and review arrangements for the Welsh funding framework. Progress on implementation and operation will be reported to the UK Parliament and National Assembly for Wales through 'annual Wales Act 2014 implementation reports'. The agreement is also to be reviewed periodically: 'The first review will take place before the end of the block grant funding transitional period, and may include input from independent bodies.' Either government can request a review, but not more than once per Assembly or Parliamentary term. This gives a reporting channel, a review timetable and a limit on review frequency. However, it names no success measures or outcomes to be measured, so there is no indication of how we would know the policy has worked. The reporting concerns implementation, not impact. There is no mention of testing the policy first, nor any reason why testing would be inappropriate, and no evaluation design or consultation plan. The strongest argument for a higher level is that the review and annual reporting resemble an evaluation plan with a timetable and possible independent input. But that is process monitoring, with no measures, so it does not clearly reach Level 1. Because it gives no success measures, I score it 0. To reach Level 1 the document would need to say what outcomes the funding arrangements are expected to achieve and how they will be judged. For Level 2 it would also need to say what the review will assess, who will carry it out, and how the policy was tested.
